title: Exact tree synchronization certificates and observable phase information
status: Full nondegenerate tree branch classification and quantitative bounds proved here; rational examples verified; no general cyclic or global-convergence claim
summary: A finite tree makes the nonlinear locking problem unusually exact: every edge flow is fixed by a cut sum, the cohesive phase differences follow by arcsine, and stability is certified by a positive weighted Laplacian. The same calculation separates dynamic stability from observability. Relative-phase measurements lose common phase and common frequency, while even a stable synchronized star has exact nonlinear motions invisible to a center-only sensor. The locking criterion is classical; the derivation, rational certificate, sensitivity bounds and observation examples here are an explicit synthesis, not a claim of a newly discovered synchronization theorem.
definitions: Let T=(V,E) be an undirected connected tree with n≥2 vertices, arbitrarily oriented edges and incidence matrix B∈R^(n×(n−1)). A column has −1 at its tail and +1 at its head. Every edge has coupling K_e>0.
Use the symmetric Kuramoto equation θ̇=ω−B diag(K)sin(Bᵀθ), componentwise sine. Since 1ᵀB=0, mean frequency is Ω=(1/n)1ᵀω. In the rotating frame set b=ω−Ω1, so 1ᵀb=0 and θ̇=b−B diag(K)sin(Bᵀθ).

General phase states lie on (R/2πZ)^n modulo the diagonal common-phase circle. A cohesive lift has δ=Bᵀθ with |δ_e|<π/2. Fixing 1ᵀθ=0 removes the common-phase direction locally. For 0<γ<π/2 one can instead impose the closed bound |δ_e|≤γ.
For each oriented edge e, remove it and let H_e be the component containing its head. Define the cut flow f_e=Σ_(i∈H_e)b_i. At a locked state the flow equation is Bf=b.
The linearization at a cohesive locked state is η̇=−L_wη, where L_w=B diag(w)Bᵀ and w_e=K_e cosδ_e=√(K_e²−f_e²)>0. Let λ₂ denote the least positive Laplacian eigenvalue.

result.name: Necessary and sufficient tree locking, local stability, boundary sensitivity and observability
result.statement: If every |f_e|<K_e, there are exactly 2^(n−1) locked equilibria on the phase torus modulo common phase. Each edge independently selects arcsin(f_e/K_e) or π−arcsin(f_e/K_e), modulo 2π. An equilibrium with q negative edge cosines has exactly q unstable linear directions on the phase quotient; there are C(n−1,q) such equilibria. Thus precisely one branch, with all edge cosines positive, is locally exponentially stable and cohesive. A state with |δ_e|≤γ<π/2 exists exactly when |f_e|≤K_e sinγ for every edge. If any |f_e|>K_e there is no locked equilibrium; if exactly r edges saturate and the others are strictly feasible, the count becomes 2^(n−1−r) and the quotient Hessian has r zero directions. For the stable branch, edge-flow sensitivity is ∂δ_e/∂f_e=1/w_e. The rate bounds are min_e(w_e)λ₂(BBᵀ)≤λ₂(L_w)≤n w_e/[s(n−s)] for every edge separating s and n−s vertices. A full relative-phase panel leaves only common phase unobservable and a uniform natural-frequency shift unidentifiable; a restricted center-only star sensor can miss additional exact nonlinear trajectories.
result.proof:
First prove the cut formula. A connected tree has n−1 edges and B has full column rank. One elementary proof removes a leaf: a zero-divergence flow has zero flow on its only incident edge, and induction removes all edges. The column image is contained in 1⊥ and has dimension n−1, so it equals 1⊥. Thus Bf=b has exactly one solution. Summing the divergence equation over H_e cancels every internal edge and leaves +f_e at the unique crossing edge, giving the displayed cut sum. Conversely those sums produce the unique solution; this can also be constructed by repeatedly eliminating leaves. No nonlinear approximation has been made.

At an equilibrium, f_e=K_e sinδ_e. Strict cohesion forces |f_e|<K_e and gives the unique principal value δ_e=arcsin(f_e/K_e). On a tree, any collection of real edge differences lifts to node phases: choose a root phase and integrate differences along the unique root-to-node path. There are no cycle-sum compatibility conditions. Subtracting the node mean fixes the chosen gauge. This proves sufficiency and uniqueness modulo common phase. Replacing the interval by [−γ,γ] gives precisely |f_e|≤K_e sinγ because sine is strictly increasing there. For a graph with cycles, the integration step can fail even when individual edge bounds hold, so this proof must not be extended merely by reusing its inequalities.

For the full branch classification, consider phase differences modulo 2π rather than restricting to the principal interval. Each strict scalar equation sinδ_e=f_e/K_e has exactly two distinct circle solutions, with cosines of opposite sign. A tree integrates every edge assignment uniquely modulo common phase, so there are exactly 2^(n−1) equilibria. On 1⊥ the linear map T=Bᵀ is an isomorphism. The quotient Hessian quadratic form is x↦(Tx)ᵀdiag(K_e cosδ_e)(Tx), and Sylvester’s law of inertia therefore gives exactly one negative direction per negative edge cosine, one positive direction per positive cosine and one zero direction per saturated edge. The dynamics has the negative of this Hessian as its Jacobian, so q negative cosines give q unstable eigenvalues. Choosing the q negative branches among n−1 edges gives C(n−1,q). All-positive cosines give the unique local minimum; every other nondegenerate branch is a saddle or the all-negative repeller. If r edges saturate, each of those sine equations has only one circle solution, giving 2^(n−1−r) equilibria with r extra linear zero directions. These boundary statements classify the algebraic count and Hessian inertia only; higher-order behavior at a zero eigenvalue is not inferred.

For local stability, differentiate the vector field. Its negative Jacobian is L_w. For every x, xᵀL_wx=Σ_e w_e(Bᵀx)_e². With positive w and connected T, this vanishes exactly when x is constant. Hence the common-phase eigenvalue is zero and every mean-zero eigenvalue is positive. This proves transverse linear stability, and the nonlinear conclusion follows directly from a local gradient estimate. On a mean-zero cohesive lift define U(θ)=−bᵀθ−Σ_e K_e cos((Bᵀθ)_e); the rotating-frame dynamics is −∇U. Around a strict cohesive equilibrium choose a sufficiently small convex ball inside a domain |δ_e|≤γ<π/2. Its Hessian is bounded below on 1⊥ by mI with m=cosγ·λ₂(B diag(K)Bᵀ)>0. If x=θ−θ*, then d||x||²/dt≤−2m||x||² in that ball. The vector field points inward on its boundary, so sufficiently near initial states stay there and converge at least as e^(−mt). This is a local argument; no invariance or attraction of the entire cohesive domain has been assumed.

Differentiate arcsin(f_e/K_e) while holding K_e fixed to get ∂δ_e/∂f_e=1/√(K_e²−f_e²)=1/w_e. Because f_e is a linear cut sum of b, this also gives exact frequency sensitivities. Holding the other flows fixed and changing only f_e shifts the phases by a constant on each component of the cut. In the mean-zero gauge, the two constants differ by dδ_e; therefore ||∂θ/∂f_e||₂=√(s(n−s)/n)/w_e. Thus sensitivity diverges as an edge saturates, even though the equilibrium remains locally stable before the boundary.

The rate estimates quantify the same boundary. The inequality L_w≽w_min BBᵀ gives λ₂(L_w)≥w_min λ₂(BBᵀ) by the Rayleigh principle on 1⊥. For the upper bound, use a test vector equal to (n−s)/n on a component of size s and −s/n on the other. Its only nonzero edge difference is one across the removed edge, its squared norm is s(n−s)/n and its energy is w_e. Its Rayleigh quotient is n w_e/[s(n−s)], proving the bound. If one bridge weight tends to zero, the convergence rate therefore tends to zero; the tree is dynamically approaching disconnection in its linearized restoring force.

For observability, let A=−L_w and C=Bᵀ. Then ker C=span{1}, A1=0, and the unobservable linear subspace ⋂_(j≥0)ker(CA^j) is exactly span{1}: the j=0 kernel already gives an upper bound, while common phase survives every power. For sine measurements the local derivative is diag(cosδ*)Bᵀ, whose diagonal factor is invertible under strict cohesion, so the same conclusion holds. Adding an absolute phase measurement e_rᵀ makes the stacked instantaneous observation injective. Separately, replacing ω by ω+c1 changes a solution to θ(t)+ct1 and leaves every relative-phase output unchanged. Relative data can identify b but cannot determine Ω without a time or phase reference.

A stronger blindness example does not rely on common phase. Take a star with center 1 and identical coupling k>0, equal natural frequencies removed by a rotating frame, and at least two leaves. Put θ₁(t)=0, θ₀(t)=a(t), θ₂(t)=−a(t), and all other leaf phases zero, where ȧ=−k sin a. The center receives sin a+sin(−a)=0, and each leaf equation is satisfied. For |a₀|<π, a(t)=2 arctan(tan(a₀/2)e^(−kt)) is an exact solution converging to synchronization. Its center output is identically zero, just as for the equilibrium, so arbitrarily close nonequilibrium states are not identifiable from that output. At linear order, leaf vectors with zero center and zero leaf sum form an (n−2)-dimensional invisible eigenspace with eigenvalue −k. Adding a measurement of one displaced leaf or one of its incident edges detects this particular pair motion, while measuring every edge difference detects all mean-zero states. Thus local convergence and local observability are independent properties even within an exactly solvable stable family.

example.setup: Use vertices 0,1,2,3 with edges oriented 0→1, 1→2, 1→3. Let Ω=2, b=(−1/2,1/6,1/3,0), ω=(3/2,13/6,7/3,2), couplings K=(5/6,13/15,1/2), and cut flows f=(1/2,1/3,0). These are rational input data.
example.calculation:
The incidence equation is Bf=(−f₀,f₀−f₁−f₂,f₁,f₂)=b. The edge sines are s=(3/5,5/13,0), and choose positive cosines c=(4/5,12/13,1). The exact unit phasors are z₀=1, z₁=(4+3i)/5, z₂=(33+56i)/65 and z₃=(4+3i)/5. Their head-tail ratios have precisely those rational real and imaginary parts. Equivalently, choose phases (0,α,α+β,α), where α=arctan(3/4) and β=arctan(5/12), before subtracting the mean. All edge differences are principal and even satisfy |sinδ_e|<4/5, a strict certificate for the cohesive bound γ=arcsin(4/5).

The Hessian weights are w=Kc=(2/3,4/5,1/2). Every principal cofactor of the stable weighted tree Laplacian equals their product 4/15, and its kernel is exactly the common-phase line. The unweighted four-node star has λ₂=1, so the transverse rate obeys 1/2≤λ₂(L_w)≤2/3, the upper bound using the leaf-3 cut. These bounds and the rational Laplacian entries can be checked without evaluating any inverse trigonometric function. Flipping any subset of the three edge cosine signs, while leaving the sine values fixed, constructs all eight phase-locked branches with rational phasors. Their unstable dimensions have counts 1,3,3,1 for indices 0,1,2,3; the stable branch is the sole index-zero case.

Now retain K and the first two flows but replace f₂ by q∈(−1/2,1/2). This changes b to (−1/2,1/6−q,1/3,q). The third weight is w₂(q)=√(1/4−q²), which is always the minimum weight. Consequently w₂(q)≤λ₂(L_w(q))≤(4/3)w₂(q), while dδ₂/dq=1/w₂(q) and the mean-zero phase sensitivity norm is √3/(2w₂(q)). Thus λ₂ times the edge-phase sensitivity stays between 1 and 4/3, while the rate vanishes and sensitivity diverges at either saturation boundary. The rational parametrization q=t/(1+t²), w₂=(1−t²)/(2(1+t²)) for 0≤t<1 supplies exact examples arbitrarily close to the boundary.
example.conclusion: The nonlinear equilibrium, its positive Hessian and its cut-flow certificate are explicit. The parameter family proves a quantitative relation between critical slowing and ill-conditioned phase reconstruction. The separate exact star trajectory proves that a stable network can still be invisible to an inadequate observation panel.

limits: The theorem covers symmetric positive couplings on a finite tree and a specified principal cohesive lift. It does not assert global convergence, attraction from arbitrary phases, robustness to noise or delays, or sufficiency of edge bounds on general cycles. At a saturated edge |f_e|=K_e the positive-weight and exponential-stability proof fails; existence at the closed π/2 boundary does not restore its missing rate. The rational verifier certifies finite examples and exact identities, not the general theorem in a proof assistant. The tree-locking criterion is established literature; no novelty claim is made for it.
extension: The completed operational consequence is a two-stage certificate: first verify Bf=b and edge feasibility to certify a cohesive equilibrium; then verify the rank of the actual observation map on the mean-zero state space. For a full edge panel the residual blindness is exactly common phase, whereas a center-only symmetric-star panel fails even for exact nonlinear trajectories. If a graph contains cycles, an additional cycle-compatibility problem must be solved before reusing this certificate design.
